'''David Olmstead Conover''' (born August 26, 1953)<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Vm1VAAAAMAAJ |title=House of Hünerhoff: American saga of a Westfalen family |last=Kelley |first=Elizabeth Conover |date=1987 |publisher=Harlo |isbn=9780818701016 |pages=275 |language=en}}</ref> is an American marine biologist and professor in the School of Marine and Atmospheric Sciences at [[Stony Brook University]]. He was the Vice President for Research at Stony Brook University and operations manager for the SUNY Research Foundation, and until his retirement in 2020 he was vice president for Research and Innovation at the [[University of Oregon]].<ref name="uo">{{cite web |last1=Schill |first1=Michael |title=David Conover, vice president for research and innovation, to step down in July 2020 |url=https://provost.uoregon.edu/david-conover-vice-president-research-and-innovation-step-down-july-2020 |website=University of Oregon |access-date=6 September 2022}}</ref> He is known for his research on the ecology of marine fishes and [[fisheries]].<ref name=research>{{Cite web |url=http://research.stonybrook.edu/dr-david-o-conover |title=Dr. David O. Conover |website=research.stonybrook.edu |access-date=2017-08-02 |archive-date=August 2, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170802204828/http://research.stonybrook.edu/dr-david-o-conover |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=5434698 |title=Ocean Fishing May Spread 'Runt' Genes |last=Malakoff |first=David |date=2006-05-27 |website=NPR.org |language=en |access-date=2017-08-03}}</ref> His son is [[Adam Conover]], host of ''[[Adam Ruins Everything]]'', and his daughter is [[Emily Conover]], scientific journalist at [[Science News]].

==Career==
David O. Conover joined the faculty of Stony Brook University in 1981 as an assistant professor. In 1995, he was named Associate Dean of Marine Sciences. In 1997, he was named the first Mote Eminent Scholar Chair in fisheries ecology.<ref name=research/> From 2003 to 2010, he was the dean of the [[School of Marine and Atmospheric Sciences]] at Stony Brook University,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.somas.stonybrook.edu/people/employee-history/ |title=Employee History |date=2016-02-24 |website=SoMAS |language=en-US |access-date=2017-08-02}}</ref> after which he became director of the [[National Science Foundation]]'s division of ocean sciences, while remaining on the faculty at Stony Brook.<ref>{{Cite press release |title=SBU Dean of the School of Marine Sciences Appointed NSF Director, Division of Ocean Sciences |date=2010-04-28 |publisher=Stony Brook University |url=http://www.somas.stonybrook.edu/2010/04/28/sbu-dean-of-the-school-of-marine-sciences-appointed-nsf-director-division-of-ocean-sciences/ |access-date=August 17, 2017 |archive-date=August 17, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170817120418/http://www.somas.stonybrook.edu/2010/04/28/sbu-dean-of-the-school-of-marine-sciences-appointed-nsf-director-division-of-ocean-sciences/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2013, he left the National Science Foundation, and was named Interim Vice President for Research at Stony Brook; he became vice president for Research there two years later.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://sb.cc.stonybrook.edu/news/general/2015-01-14-david-conover-vp-for-research.php |title=David O. Conover Named Vice President for Research at Stony Brook University |date=2015-01-14 |website=sb.cc.stonybrook.edu |access-date=2017-08-02 |archive-date=August 3, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170803004940/http://sb.cc.stonybrook.edu/news/general/2015-01-14-david-conover-vp-for-research.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> Also in 2015, he received the [[Oscar E. Sette]] Award from the [[American Fisheries Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.stonybrook.edu/happenings/alumni/david-conover-to-receive-national-award-for-excellence-in-marine-fishery-biology/ |title=David Conover to Receive National Award for Excellence in Marine Fishery Biology |date=2015-07-02 |website=Stony Brook Matters |language=en-US |access-date=2017-08-02}}</ref>

In 2016, he became the Vice President for Research and Innovation at the University of Oregon. He retired in 2020.<ref name=uo/>

On October 27, 2015, Conover appeared as himself in the fifth episode of his son Adam's television series on [[TruTV]], ''[[Adam Ruins Everything]]''.
